findings.kind: TikZ diagram fails to render in ItemBody
findings.excerpt: The Example introduces two depth-one CART trees for the mixed bootstrap case, then supplies a tikzpicture with two positioned root nodes and child leaves.
findings.symptom: The matching local HTML and both assigned screenshot tiles show a red “diagram failed to render” block containing the raw TikZ source instead of the two trees. The receipt records this diagram failure. The tree labels and left/right split interpretation in the source agree with the stated training points; the independent finite-count verification remains legible.
checks: Viewed screenshots/ex-random-forest-zero-margin-vote-limit--01.png and --02.png individually at original resolution; the first tile shows the raw diagram failure block and the second shows the remainder of the verification.
Compared the complete source ItemBody lines 33–48 with the matching local HTML; the prose and verification render, while the TikZ block does not.
Verified the screenshot hashes against the revision-2 receipt; the receipt lists the same TikZ source in diagram_failures.
findings.suggested_repair: Rewrite the two trees using a TikZ form supported by the local renderer (for example, separate tree scopes with explicitly anchored roots), then regenerate the matching HTML and inspect every resulting tile.

diagram_review.scope: Reviewed assigned titles and complete ItemBody text, all displayed formulas and TikZ, and whether the mathematical content would materially benefit from a missing diagram. Checked the two tree cases in the random-forest example and the causal DAG pair in the PC example against their stated variables, edge directions, split rules, and proof/verification relations.
diagram_review.notes: The random-forest tree diagram is present in source but fails to render; this is recorded as a rendering defect, not as a missing-diagram candidate. The PC latent-confounding DAG diagram renders and matches the two structural models described. No other missing diagram was sufficiently high-likelihood to report.
